introduction: Hetty the Hen has news. She almost always has news. The trough is low again, and she has a theory about whose fault that is. She has not quite worked out yet that you are the donkey she is talking about.

logicalFallacies.explanation: Attacking the animal instead of the argument. Whether Rue arrived in a mud cart has nothing to do with whether the pond is muddy.

sentences.text: Morning! Did you hear? That new donkey — Rue, I think it is — has been complaining about the pond drain again.
I wouldn't put much stock in it, mind. He arrived in a mud cart with straw in his ears; he's hardly the sort who'd know about water.

logicalFallacies.explanation: The claim is about the pond. Hetty answers it by describing how Rue turned up and what he looks like, which tells us nothing about the water.

sentences.text: Anyway, the pond's been going brown since before the frost.
The grate at the outflow is bent, you know. I saw it myself, chasing a beetle.
Water backs up behind it, so the mud goes into the pond instead of out of it.
Someone ought to tell the Flock. They don't much listen to hens.

steps.message:
This is **[accent]not a debate[/accent]** — no sides, no moderator, no score.

Two animals are talking. Your only job is to **[accent]catch the bad reasoning[/accent]**.
Open the **[accent]magnifying glass[/accent]** to read what was said, sentence by sentence.

**[warning]Continue is locked[/warning]** until you judge it.

Tag a fallacy — or press **[accent]Clean[/accent]**. Not every sentence is a trap.
